title: Result Clauses
subtitle: tam fortis est ut omnēs eum laudent. Consequence, not purpose.
objectives: Recognize result clauses with ut + subjunctive preceded by a signal word (tam, ita, tālis, tantus).
Distinguish result from purpose by signal word and meaning.

sections.heading: Result clauses
sections.body:
Result clauses express the consequence of an action. They use ut + subjunctive, preceded by a signal word:
  tam (so), ita (so, thus), tālis (such), tantus (so great)

tam fortis est ut omnēs eum laudent. — He is so brave that everyone praises him.
tanta tempestās fuit ut nāvēs dēlerentur. — There was so great a storm that the ships were destroyed.

Caesar writes: tanta vīs aquae ēruptiōnem fēcit ut mūrum perfringeret. — So great a force of water broke out that it shattered the wall.

items.prompt: Translate: tam celer est ut nēmō eum capere possit.
items.answer: He is so fast that no one can catch him.
Result has a signal word (tam, ita, etc.) and describes consequence, not intent.

words.gloss: He spoke in such a way that everyone believed.
